title: Инсценировка похищения и звонок отцу  (The Staged Kidnapping and the Ransom Call)

segments.t: A mysterious caller phones Nastya's father and demands a hefty ransom that very evening if he wants to see his daughter unharmed. Once the call ends, it is revealed that Nastya is sitting comfortably with her homeless shelter friends, having staged the entire kidnapping herself.
Но мы хотим получить за нее много денег.
Ну, а так все по плану.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Nastya. Little Nastya.' Reacting boldly on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Good evening once again.' Senya warmly uses this evening greeting as they meet using "dobryy vecher" ("good evening") — the standard Russian evening hello, literally "good evening".
'Where is my daughter?' Mentioning her daughter beside Senya, Nastya chooses "doch" ("daughter") so Senya gets the point right away.
Но мы хотим получить за нее много денег.
'We want to receive a lot of money for her.' Emphasizing the money right here, Senya chooses "poluchit" ("to get, to receive") so Nastya gets the point right away.
'This very day.' Nastya pushes back pointedly with a smile, testing Senya's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
'How much is a lot?' Senya opens up briskly at once and lands on "mnogo" ("a lot") as the key everyday word here.
'How much do we need?' Holding firm naturally in this beat, Nastya leans on "nuzhno" ("it is needed, one has to"), which carries the whole predicate in Russian without needing "it is".
'It is me.' Senya weighs in candidly with a smile, letting the remark speak for itself.
'And right now.' Holding firm naturally right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Your daughter is going to suffer.' Leaning in dryly at once, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'My compliments to you.' Nastya proceeds steadily with Senya, so Senya knows she is not just making small talk.
Ну, а так все по плану.
'Well, otherwise everything is going according to plan.' Focusing on the plan in this beat, Senya centers the thought on "planu" ("plan", from "plan") without wasting a word.
'You will collect the money from my dad.' Bringing up the money around Senya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Но мы хотим получить за нее много денег.
Ну, а так все по плану.

That wraps up this scene as nastya's father receives a ransom call demanding a large sum of money that very day, revealing that Nastya staged her own kidnapping with her homeless friends. Until next time!
